Explore top resources for students seeking funding.","keywords":[],"articleBody":"Even the best student loans and other financial aid items don't always provide enough to cover all the costs of an average college tuition. Scholarships are a great way to bridge the gap, with no obligation to repay the money. Finding the ones you qualify for can be difficult, but several great scholarship websites can help you do it. However, remember that many colleges deduct private scholarships from the amount of gift aid they provide, reducing how much \"free money\" you can get from the school. That would effectively negate the work you did in seeking out and applying for private scholarships. Therefore, you should consider looking at schools that offer merit-based scholarships or provide generous packages to students with financial need. Below are our top 10 picks for the best scholarship websites of 2025. Scholarship websites help you find opportunities that can save you thousands of dollars on your education. A wide range of scholarships are available, from local scholarships to national awards for students in niche categories. By filtering your searches on a scholarship website for criteria like location, race, and GPA, you can quickly identify the specific opportunities available to you. Scholarship websites aren't just for unearthing opportunities. Many will also help you apply for scholarships and track the progress of your applications. We've rounded up the best scholarship websites for students looking to save on the cost of college, emphasizing those that provide a wide breadth of opportunities. Most of the sites are free to use. Some offer basic features at no cost, with an option to pay for additional functionality. Scholarships.com uses an algorithm to pair you with scholarships you may be eligible for, with millions of opportunities available. To make the algorithm work for you, you'll need to create an account and input your current grade in school, your birthday, ZIP code, and email address. You can also search through its database of scholarships yourself, filtering by criteria such as academic major, GPA, and military affiliation. The website is free to use. Similar to Scholarships.com, Fastweb has an algorithm that uses your profile on its website to match you each day with scholarships you may want to apply for. Fastweb has more than 1.5 million scholarship opportunities. Fastweb's scholarship opportunities are updated daily, so check back frequently to see if you qualify for the latest batch. Professional scholarship researchers vet every scholarship in its database. The website is free to use. Bold.org partners with donors to create scholarships, grants, and fellowships for students who qualify. The interface is sleek, and the website offers exclusive scholarships you won't find elsewhere. You can explore scholarships by category. For instance, Bold.org has a tab for nursing students, women, and students from Texas. Bold.org even has a button you can toggle to search for scholarships that don't require essays. The website is free to use. CollegeBoard is probably best known for its administration of college entry exams and Advanced Placement programs, but it also has a tool to help you find scholarships. Its BigFuture website has a database of more than 6,000 scholarship opportunities. After you make an account, you can search for opportunities through various filters. This includes scholarships available for children of divorced parents, non-citizens, and students who are members of some community organizations. The BigFuture search tool is free to use. Going Merry, from the same company offering Earnest student loans, will autofill some scholarship forms once you've input the required information, saving you time in the process and allowing you to apply to multiple scholarships simultaneously. Additionally, it will help you keep on top of deadlines by sending reminders about when applications are due. The website is also a great source for local awards, which may be harder to find on other scholarship websites. Going Merry even has a mobile app — perfect for students who want to manage scholarship applications on the go. Going Merry is free to use. Sallie Mae acquired Scholly in July 2023 and renamed the website Scholarship Search by Sallie. The original Scholly website gained a premier reputation after appearing on the hit show Shark Tank. The scholarship search website will pair you with scholarships and give them a score. The higher the score, the better you fit the scholarship's requirements. Sallie Mae also made the website completely free for all students, families, and other users. Previously, some premium features, including personalized scholarship matches, cost money to use, with pricing ranging from $4.99 for one month to $34.99 for a year subscription. ScholarshipOwl is another freemium service. While you can use a portion of the website for free, you'll have to pay to access some features, including a personal account manager and the automatic submission of applications. ScholarshipOwl uses AI to help students win more scholarships. The premium package offers tools and strategies such as credibility scores for each provider, automatic reapplications, exclusive verified scholarships, and information on how much competition students have for each scholarship. While the premium service can range from $20 to $69 a month, with the highest tier, you'll have access to several hours of college admissions webinars and an expert who will proofread one 500-word essay a month. ProFellow is a website that focuses exclusively on funding awards for graduate and professional development. The website has a database of more than 2,800 available opportunities. ProFellow also offers workshops, courses, and other events on how to create an application that stands out. It's free to use and is a great place for people who have already completed their undergraduate degrees to begin their search. Formerly known as \"Cappex,\" Appily is more than just a scholarship website. It's a comprehensive platform for researching schools, understanding college applications, and adjusting to college life. The scholarship portion of the Appily site is simple and user-friendly. Start by creating a free account to gain access. From there, you can search for scholarships by filtering for criteria like location, ethnicity, and minimum award amount. Once you've found a scholarship you like, you can save it to your account or apply immediately. Niche is another comprehensive website for researching colleges and finding scholarships. It allows you to search for scholarships by category or quickly get matched with the opportunities that you're eligible for. Niche stands out from other scholarship websites by offering \"easy to apply\" as a search filter, which allows you to search specifically for scholarships that don't require essays or letters of recommendation. Niche is free to use. \"Scholarship\" is a broad term that applies to various financial awards for students. Before applying for scholarships, it's best to understand which types of scholarships are available to you. Here's a quick breakdown of the main types of scholarships you'll find on scholarship websites. Merit-based scholarships are awarded to students who display a high level of achievement in academics or extracurricular activities. These opportunities are especially worth pursuing if you have a high GPA, strong standardized test scores, or a special talent. Need-based scholarships are awarded to students who show they require financial assistance to afford the cost of higher education. In many cases, need-based financial packages are called \"grants\" rather than \"scholarships.\" Some scholarships are reserved for members of marginalized identity groups. Eligibility for these scholarships depends on categories like race, ethnicity, age, sexual identity, and gender. Field-specific scholarships are awarded to students pursuing a particular field or major. These scholarships represent a great opportunity for students who already know what they plan to study. A scholarship website is a tool, and, like any tool, it's most effective if you know how to use it. Here are tips for getting the most out of scholarship websites: The effort you put into the scholarship application process can majorly impact your success rate. To maximize your chances of earning scholarships, keep these tips in mind. Your essay or personal statement gives you a chance to address the scholarship committee directly. To win them over, make sure you deliver a piece of writing that's thoughtful and polished. While each scholarship may have its own specifications, it's generally best to discuss how you've overcome any struggles in your life, the goals you hope to meet, and how achieving your goals will positively impact society. A strong letter of recommendation corroborates what you say about yourself, showing the scholarship committee that you're a deserving candidate. Make sure you request recommendation letters from the right people — starting with teachers, coaches, and supervisors who can speak to your character or personal growth. Also, be sure to ask these people for recommendation letters in advance and in a polite and professional way. Respecting their time will reinforce their positive opinion of you, which could influence how they describe you in the letter. Scammers will sometimes ask for money in exchange for a scholarship opportunity. For example, you receive a letter, email, or message saying you're a finalist for a scholarship, but you need to pay a \"processing fee\" to maintain your eligibility. Ignore these messages and stick with legitimate scholarship applications that don't ask you to pay. You probably can't get a 100% scholarship, as most private scholarships won't completely cover the cost of your education. You're better off looking for merit scholarships from individual colleges that cover your costs completely or filling out the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) to see if you're eligible for a need-based full ride. If entering the first year of undergrad, it is best to start applying for scholarships during the summer break before senior year. The timing of when you should start filling out applications for scholarships varies depending on the specific scholarship you're applying for. Some scholarships are even available to high school students, so it's never too early to start your search. The GPA requirement varies from scholarship to scholarship, but the lowest GPA is usually around 2.0. In general, you'll have a better chance of success with a higher GPA. To find a trustworthy scholarship, do your due diligence. Confirm that the scholarship's sponsor is legitimate by looking at reviews of the company and checking its Better Business Bureau grade, if available. To increase your chances of winning a scholarship, use scholarship websites that allow you to identify various opportunities. You can also boost your applications by crafting a strong essay or personal statement and securing excellent letters of recommendation. We consulted scholarship and financial experts to give their insights into finding the best scholarship websites — and when to avoid them altogether. Neeta Vallab: \"Honestly, there are very limited advantages to using private scholarships over grants directly from schools. Unlike private scholarships, most grants from schools do not require a separate application and are renewable for four years. Additionally, many colleges will deduct the value of a private scholarship from any award they give you. This is called 'displacement.' And because this practice is so prevalent, it often leaves students with no net financial benefit, despite the effort they invested in submitting an application.\" Jennifer Ledwith: \"Unlike scholarships from schools, private scholarships can be used at multiple universities. Furthermore, unlike grants from schools, private scholarships don't have to follow federal or institutional financial aid methodology. Consequently, students can receive private scholarships without regard to other financial aid awards. Furthermore, some private scholarships send the money directly to the student, allowing greater flexibility in using the funds.\" Christopher Rim: \"No, you should never pick a loan over a scholarship! They should be absolutely sure to read the terms of their scholarship thoroughly to understand the possible consequences if they fail to meet the set conditions.\" Ryan Wangman: \"You'll need to repay the money you borrow from any lender, so it's never a good idea to choose a loan over a scholarship, which is money you don't have to pay back. Rim: \"Many websites will allow students to filter through their databases to find scholarships they are eligible for. Not all merit scholarship information is published however.\" Ledwith: \"Students should keep a spreadsheet to track their scholarship application status.\" Wangman: \"Like Jennifer mentioned, a spreadsheet is usually the best way to track application status.                 <div class="table-of-contents table-of-contents-sticky" data-analytics-module="jump-to" data-type="custom"></div><p>Even the <a target="_self" href="https://www.businessinsider.com/personal-finance/student-loans/best-private-student-loans" data-track-click="{"element_name":"body_link","event":"tout_click","index":"bi_value_unassigned","product_field":"bi_value_unassigned"}" rel="">best student loans</a> and other financial aid items don't always provide enough to cover all the costs of an <a target="_self" class="" href="https://www.businessinsider.com/personal-finance/student-loans/average-college-tuition" data-track-click="{"element_name":"body_link","event":"tout_click","index":"bi_value_unassigned","product_field":"bi_value_unassigned"}" rel="">average college tuition</a>. Scholarships are a great way to bridge the gap, with no obligation to repay the money. Finding the ones you qualify for can be difficult, but several great scholarship websites can help you do it.</p><p>However, remember that many colleges deduct private scholarships from the amount of gift aid they provide, reducing how much "free money" you can get from the school. That would effectively negate the work you did in seeking out and applying for private scholarships. Therefore, you should consider looking at schools that offer <a target="_self" class="" href="https://www.businessinsider.com/personal-finance/student-loans/what-is-merit-scholarship" data-track-click="{"element_name":"body_link","event":"tout_click","index":"bi_value_unassigned","product_field":"bi_value_unassigned"}" rel="">merit-based scholarships</a> or provide generous packages to students with financial need.</p><p>Below are our top 10 picks for the best scholarship websites of 2025.</p><h3 id="best-scholarship-websites" data-toc-id="c5634d5a-33b9-4446-8020-0899fbf55dbb" data-toc-label="Best Scholarship Websites" class="toc-anchor">Best Scholarship Websites of 2025</h3><ul><li>Scholarships.com</li><li>Fastweb</li><li>Bold.org</li><li>BigFuture by CollegeBoard</li><li>GoingMerry by Earnest</li><li>Scholarship Search by Sallie</li><li>ScholarshipOwl</li><li>ProFellow</li><li>Appily</li><li>Niche</li></ul><h2 id="86c01e23-1490-4bf9-a3d9-bb47ebdef2e4" data-toc-id="86c01e23-1490-4bf9-a3d9-bb47ebdef2e4"><strong>Why Use Scholarship Websites?</strong></h2><p>Scholarship websites help you find opportunities that can save you thousands of dollars on your education. A wide range of scholarships are available, from local scholarships to national awards for students in niche categories. By filtering your searches on a scholarship website for criteria like location, race, and GPA, you can quickly identify the specific opportunities available to you. </p><p>Scholarship websites aren't just for unearthing opportunities. Many will also help you apply for scholarships and track the progress of your applications.</p><h2 id="compare-the-best-scholarship-websites" data-toc-id="74222a66-790f-4fd0-938d-4a46393370f4" data-toc-label="Compare the Best Scholarship Websites" class="toc-anchor">Compare the Best Scholarship Websites</h2><p>We've rounded up the best scholarship websites for students looking to save on the cost of college, emphasizing those that provide a wide breadth of opportunities. Most of the sites are free to use. Some offer basic features at no cost, with an option to pay for additional functionality.</p><h3 id="118bef61-c5e1-4c8e-b262-a1c234d45e70" data-toc-id="118bef61-c5e1-4c8e-b262-a1c234d45e70">Scholarships.com</h3><p><a target="_blank" rel="noopener nofollow" href="https://www.scholarships.com/" data-track-click="{"click_type":"other","element_name":"body_link","event":"outbound_click"}">Scholarships.com</a> uses an algorithm to pair you with scholarships you may be eligible for, with millions of opportunities available. To make the algorithm work for you, you'll need to create an account and input your current grade in school, your birthday, ZIP code, and email address.</p><p>You can also search through its database of scholarships yourself, filtering by criteria such as academic major, GPA, and military affiliation. The website is free to use.</p><h3 id="81b1f975-4bd9-4969-959a-f35e63affdac" data-toc-id="81b1f975-4bd9-4969-959a-f35e63affdac">Fastweb</h3><p>Similar to Scholarships.com, <a target="_blank" rel="noopener nofollow" href="https://www.fastweb.com/" data-track-click="{"click_type":"other","element_name":"body_link","event":"outbound_click"}">Fastweb</a> has an algorithm that uses your profile on its website to match you each day with scholarships you may want to apply for. Fastweb has more than 1.5 million scholarship opportunities.</p><p>Fastweb's scholarship opportunities are updated daily, so check back frequently to see if you qualify for the latest batch. Professional scholarship researchers vet every scholarship in its database. The website is free to use.</p><h3 id="4c2744da-7330-40f1-80e4-d8ba0788ec15" data-toc-id="4c2744da-7330-40f1-80e4-d8ba0788ec15">Bold.org</h3><p><a target="_blank" rel="noopener nofollow" href="https://bold.org/" data-track-click="{"click_type":"other","element_name":"body_link","event":"outbound_click"}">Bold.org</a> partners with donors to create scholarships, grants, and fellowships for students who qualify. The interface is sleek, and the website offers exclusive scholarships you won't find elsewhere.</p><p>You can explore scholarships by category. For instance, Bold.org has a tab for nursing students, women, and students from Texas. Bold.org even has a button you can toggle to search for scholarships that don't require essays. The website is free to use.</p><h3 id="19046490-f482-4ac8-9283-562f61c0a562" data-toc-id="19046490-f482-4ac8-9283-562f61c0a562">BigFuture by CollegeBoard</h3><p>CollegeBoard is probably best known for its administration of college entry exams and Advanced Placement programs, but it also has a tool to help you find scholarships. Its <a target="_blank" rel="noopener nofollow" href="https://bigfuture.collegeboard.org/" data-track-click="{"click_type":"other","element_name":"body_link","event":"outbound_click"}">BigFuture website</a> has a database of more than 6,000 scholarship opportunities.</p><p>After you make an account, you can search for opportunities through various filters. This includes scholarships available for children of divorced parents, non-citizens, and students who are members of some community organizations. The BigFuture search tool is free to use.</p><h3 id="acb46482-3e73-4a0d-94af-2142ae0c7fa2" data-toc-id="acb46482-3e73-4a0d-94af-2142ae0c7fa2">GoingMerry by Earnest</h3><p><a target="_blank" rel="noopener nofollow" href="https://goingmerry.com/" data-track-click="{"click_type":"other","element_name":"body_link","event":"outbound_click"}">Going Merry</a>, from the same company offering <a target="_self" href="https://www.businessinsider.com/personal-finance/student-loans/earnest-student-loans-review" data-track-click="{"element_name":"body_link","event":"tout_click","index":"bi_value_unassigned","product_field":"bi_value_unassigned"}" rel="">Earnest student loans</a>, will autofill some scholarship forms once you've input the required information, saving you time in the process and allowing you to apply to multiple scholarships simultaneously. Additionally, it will help you keep on top of deadlines by sending reminders about when applications are due.</p><p>The website is also a great source for local awards, which may be harder to find on other scholarship websites. Going Merry even has a mobile app — perfect for students who want to manage scholarship applications on the go. Going Merry is free to use.</p><h3 id="e7b54921-c395-4b41-b8c8-d8f6134070f9" data-toc-id="e7b54921-c395-4b41-b8c8-d8f6134070f9"><strong>Scholarship Search by Sallie</strong></h3><p>Sallie Mae acquired Scholly in July 2023 and renamed the website <a target="_blank" rel="noopener nofollow" class="" href="https://www.sallie.com/scholarships/scholly?page=1&utm_source=slmcom&utm_medium=web" data-track-click="{"click_type":"other","element_name":"body_link","event":"outbound_click"}">Scholarship Search by Sallie</a>. The original Scholly website gained a premier reputation after appearing on the hit show Shark Tank. The scholarship search website will pair you with scholarships and give them a score. The higher the score, the better you fit the scholarship's requirements.</p><p>Sallie Mae also made the website completely free for all students, families, and other users. Previously, some premium features, including personalized scholarship matches, cost money to use, with pricing ranging from $4.99 for one month to $34.99 for a year subscription.</p><h3 id="77124903-dc4b-451c-be24-fb7aca06ecb3" data-toc-id="77124903-dc4b-451c-be24-fb7aca06ecb3">ScholarshipOwl</h3><p><a target="_blank" rel="noopener nofollow" href="https://scholarshipowl.com/" data-track-click="{"click_type":"other","element_name":"body_link","event":"outbound_click"}">ScholarshipOwl</a> is another freemium service. While you can use a portion of the website for free, you'll have to pay to access some features, including a personal account manager and the automatic submission of applications.</p><p>ScholarshipOwl uses AI to help students win more scholarships. The premium package offers tools and strategies such as credibility scores for each provider, automatic reapplications, exclusive verified scholarships, and information on how much competition students have for each scholarship.</p><p>While the premium service can range from $20 to $69 a month, with the highest tier, you'll have access to several hours of college admissions webinars and an expert who will proofread one 500-word essay a month.</p><h3 id="2a127680-c7f6-46c1-9562-78e369b079c9" data-toc-id="2a127680-c7f6-46c1-9562-78e369b079c9">ProFellow</h3><p><a target="_blank" rel="noopener nofollow" href="https://www.profellow.com/" data-track-click="{"click_type":"other","element_name":"body_link","event":"outbound_click"}">ProFellow</a> is a website that focuses exclusively on funding awards for graduate and professional development. The website has a database of more than 2,800 available opportunities.</p><p>ProFellow also offers workshops, courses, and other events on how to create an application that stands out. It's free to use and is a great place for people who have already completed their undergraduate degrees to begin their search.</p><h3 id="928fad70-4acb-450d-96e5-7aedc32833d1" data-toc-id="928fad70-4acb-450d-96e5-7aedc32833d1"><strong>Appily</strong></h3><p>Formerly known as "Cappex," <a target="_blank" rel="noopener nofollow" href="https://www.appily.com/" data-track-click="{"click_type":"other","element_name":"body_link","event":"outbound_click"}">Appily</a> is more than just a scholarship website. It's a comprehensive platform for researching schools, understanding college applications, and adjusting to college life.</p><p>The scholarship portion of the Appily site is simple and user-friendly. Start by creating a free account to gain access. From there, you can search for scholarships by filtering for criteria like location, ethnicity, and minimum award amount. Once you've found a scholarship you like, you can save it to your account or apply immediately.</p><h3 id="c4bd0a43-e653-4b39-85a9-c9080886eee4" data-toc-id="c4bd0a43-e653-4b39-85a9-c9080886eee4"><strong>Niche</strong></h3><p><a target="_blank" rel="noopener nofollow" href="https://www.niche.com/" data-track-click="{"click_type":"other","element_name":"body_link","event":"outbound_click"}">Niche</a> is another comprehensive website for researching colleges and finding scholarships. It allows you to search for scholarships by category or quickly get matched with the opportunities that you're eligible for.</p><p>Niche stands out from other scholarship websites by offering "easy to apply" as a search filter, which allows you to search specifically for scholarships that don't require essays or letters of recommendation. Niche is free to use.</p><h2 id="types-of-scholarships-available" data-toc-id="33d9f529-1f9a-441e-9de3-3c1583d3cb34" data-toc-label="Types of Scholarships Available" class="toc-anchor"><strong>Types of Scholarships Available on Scholarship Websites</strong></h2><p>"Scholarship" is a broad term that applies to various financial awards for students. Before applying for scholarships, it's best to understand which types of scholarships are available to you.</p><p>Here's a quick breakdown of the main types of scholarships you'll find on scholarship websites.</p><h3 id="954726f9-93ce-4ef7-973c-932845bae842" data-toc-id="954726f9-93ce-4ef7-973c-932845bae842"><strong>Merit-Based Scholarships</strong></h3><p>Merit-based scholarships are awarded to students who display a high level of achievement in academics or extracurricular activities. These opportunities are especially worth pursuing if you have a high GPA, strong standardized test scores, or a special talent.</p><h3 id="7a9fbe43-3743-449d-87ea-ab943547a44b" data-toc-id="7a9fbe43-3743-449d-87ea-ab943547a44b"><strong>Need-Based Scholarships</strong></h3><p><a target="_self" href="https://www.businessinsider.com/personal-finance/student-loans/need-based-financial-aid" data-track-click="{"element_name":"body_link","event":"tout_click","index":"bi_value_unassigned","product_field":"bi_value_unassigned"}" rel="">Need-based scholarships</a> are awarded to students who show they require financial assistance to afford the cost of higher education. In many cases, need-based financial packages are called "grants" rather than "scholarships."</p><h3 id="ff035ceb-8272-40c5-8f40-d6267689a195" data-toc-id="ff035ceb-8272-40c5-8f40-d6267689a195"><strong>Scholarships for Minorities</strong></h3><p>Some scholarships are reserved for members of marginalized identity groups. Eligibility for these scholarships depends on categories like race, ethnicity, age, sexual identity, and gender.</p><h3 id="1a83b4f6-ad25-4f7c-a7af-dfb6a5e91ab4" data-toc-id="1a83b4f6-ad25-4f7c-a7af-dfb6a5e91ab4"><strong>Field-Specific Scholarships</strong></h3><p>Field-specific scholarships are awarded to students pursuing a particular field or major. These scholarships represent a great opportunity for students who already know what they plan to study.</p><h2 id="how-to-scholarship-websites" data-toc-id="c24247fb-fbf6-49c1-a46a-b42d3cc121d6" data-toc-label="How to Scholarship Websites" class="toc-anchor"><strong>How to Use Scholarship Websites Effectively</strong></h2><p>A scholarship website is a tool, and, like any tool, it's most effective if you know how to use it. Here are tips for getting the most out of scholarship websites:</p><ul><li><strong>Manage your profiles.</strong> You'll have to create a separate profile on every scholarship website you use. Make sure these profiles are current, and check them regularly for updates. It's also helpful to create a dedicated email address for scholarship applications. That way, a big acceptance won't get lost in your personal email.</li><li><strong>Narrow your search results.</strong> There are too many scholarships for you to look at all of them. Luckily, scholarship websites let you filter your searches by specific qualifications, including GPA, ethnicity, location, and gender. Use these filters to quickly find scholarships that work for you.</li><li><strong>Keep track of application deadlines.</strong> Each scholarship will have its own deadline to apply and it can be a struggle to hold all those dates in your head. To avoid missing out on opportunities, put these deadlines in your digital calendar and set plenty of reminders.</li></ul><h2 id="tips-for-winning-scholarships" data-toc-id="dcea593c-a5ef-4fe7-bf28-e746d0f268e8" data-toc-label="Tips for Winning Scholarships" class="toc-anchor"><strong>Tips for Winning Scholarships</strong></h2><p>The effort you put into the scholarship application process can majorly impact your success rate. To maximize your chances of earning scholarships, keep these tips in mind.</p><h3 id="6ca0f6c6-7209-4b60-ab3f-b1da829398f3" data-toc-id="6ca0f6c6-7209-4b60-ab3f-b1da829398f3"><strong>Craft a Strong Personal Statement</strong></h3><p>Your essay or personal statement gives you a chance to address the scholarship committee directly. To win them over, make sure you deliver a piece of writing that's thoughtful and polished. While each scholarship may have its own specifications, it's generally best to discuss how you've overcome any struggles in your life, the goals you hope to meet, and how achieving your goals will positively impact society.</p><h3 id="d50b1479-7710-4c5b-9376-d8c309dc4507" data-toc-id="d50b1479-7710-4c5b-9376-d8c309dc4507"><strong>Gather Excellent Letters of Recommendation</strong></h3><p>A strong letter of recommendation corroborates what you say about yourself, showing the scholarship committee that you're a deserving candidate. Make sure you request recommendation letters from the right people — starting with teachers, coaches, and supervisors who can speak to your character or personal growth. Also, be sure to ask these people for recommendation letters in advance and in a polite and professional way. Respecting their time will reinforce their positive opinion of you, which could influence how they describe you in the letter.</p><h3 id="a9a7be59-a862-4d8a-82c9-d44e5e96b300" data-toc-id="a9a7be59-a862-4d8a-82c9-d44e5e96b300"><strong>Avoid Scholarship Website Scams</strong></h3><p>Scammers will sometimes ask for money in exchange for a scholarship opportunity. For example, you receive a letter, email, or message saying you're a finalist for a scholarship, but you need to pay a "processing fee" to maintain your eligibility. Ignore these messages and stick with legitimate scholarship applications that don't ask you to pay.</p><h2 id="faqs" data-toc-id="a702f8e3-37fb-4219-8101-bec43b9d26d1" data-toc-label="FAQs" class="toc-anchor"><strong>Best Scholarship Website FAQs</strong></h2>

                </div><h2 id="5cd12770-dfa8-4169-9a72-936e974c028c" data-toc-id="5cd12770-dfa8-4169-9a72-936e974c028c">Our Experts for the Best Scholarship Websites</h2><p>We consulted scholarship and financial experts to give their insights into finding the best scholarship websites — and when to avoid them altogether.</p><ul><li>Christopher Rim, founder and CEO at Command Education</li><li>Jennifer Ledwith, owner at Scholar Ready</li><li>Neeta Vallab, founder at MeritMore</li><li>Ryan Wangman, former loans reporter at Personal Finance Insider</li></ul><h2 id="why-you-should-trust-us" data-toc-id="c2536054-1f84-423c-a167-20d8112f04da" data-toc-label="Why You Should Trust Us" class="toc-anchor">Our Experts' Advice for Choosing the Best Scholarship Websites</h2><h3 id="5f8eb0bf-cf12-4c14-b478-4c37492232c4" data-toc-id="5f8eb0bf-cf12-4c14-b478-4c37492232c4">What are the advantages of private scholarships versus scholarships or grants from schools?</h3><p><strong>Neeta Vallab: </strong></p><p>"Honestly, there are very limited advantages to using private scholarships over grants directly from schools. Unlike private scholarships, most grants from schools do not require a separate application and are renewable for four years. Additionally, many colleges will deduct the value of a private scholarship from any award they give you. This is called 'displacement.' And because this practice is so prevalent, it often leaves students with no net financial benefit, despite the effort they invested in submitting an application."</p><p><strong>Jennifer Ledwith:</strong></p><p>"Unlike scholarships from schools, private scholarships can be used at multiple universities. Furthermore, unlike grants from schools, private scholarships don't have to follow federal or institutional financial aid methodology. Consequently, students can receive private scholarships without regard to other financial aid awards. Furthermore, some private scholarships send the money directly to the student, allowing greater flexibility in using the funds."</p><h3 id="b7d26440-dd1e-401e-8290-848c45fab7f1" data-toc-id="b7d26440-dd1e-401e-8290-848c45fab7f1">Should you always consider scholarships before loans? Are there any scenarios you should pick a loan?</h3><p><strong>Christopher Rim: </strong></p><p>"No, you should never pick a loan over a scholarship! You always have to pay back loans. Students should bear in mind that they may have their scholarship rescinded if they don't meet the terms and conditions. They should be absolutely sure to read the terms of their scholarship thoroughly to understand the possible consequences if they fail to meet the set conditions."</p><p><strong>Ryan Wangman:</strong></p><p>"You'll need to repay the money you borrow from any lender, so it's never a good idea to choose a loan over a scholarship, which is money you don't have to pay back. Once students find the scholarships on databases, they should be sure to cross-check eligibility requirements on the sponsoring organization's website."</p><p><strong>Vallab</strong>: </p><p>"Private scholarships will usually have a qualifications section in their description.
